## formal
Let $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$, $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, be the composite space of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space} with its Fock inner product, $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}$ the Klein-twisted slot annihilators, $a_{1}, a_{2}$ the untwisted ones and $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ the pair annihilators. For five operators $\alpha_{1}, \dots, \alpha_{5}$ on $V$ with adjoints $\alpha_{k}^{*}$ put $\gamma_{2k-1} = \alpha_{k} + \alpha_{k}^{*}$, $\gamma_{2k} = \alpha_{k} - \alpha_{k}^{*}$, and let $G$ be the group generated by $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ and $-1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The clause is the postulates; proved.)} The $\alpha_{k}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes exactly when $\gamma_{1}, \dots, \gamma_{10}$ with $c = -1$ satisfy Premise (F2), in the form of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}, with $\gamma_{2k-1}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{2k}^{2} = c$; then $|G| = 2^{11}$, the $2^{10}$ blades $\gamma_{S}$ are trace-orthogonal on $V$, $c$ acts as $-1$ (Premise (F3)), and $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra} acts faithfully on $V$. For $(\alpha_{k}) = (\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3})$ both hold. The sign bits of the slot and the pair systems are both the operator $-1$ of $V$, so beyond the two separate systems the clause adds only (F2c) for the $24$ slot-pair pairs: clause (f) says exactly that the ten slot and pair Majorana directions are distinct directions of one group of signed directions whose sign bit acts as $-1$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The signature; proved.)} (F2) allows every signature; for Majoranas of modes it is forced, one direction of square $1$ and one of square $c$ per mode, so $(5,5)$. Its Gauss sum $\sum_{S}\gamma_{S}^{2}$ is $2^{5}$, as for $(10,0)$, so $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5) \cong \Cl_{\Z}(10,0)$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(viii)), the class of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The adjoint; proved.)} On $V$, $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ for every $g \in G$, so on the image of $\Z[G]/(c + 1)$ the adjoint is the anti-involution induced by $g \mapsto g^{-1}$; and the commutant of $G$ on the rational span of the occupation basis is the scalars, so the $G$-invariant symmetric form is the Fock form up to a scalar. The adjoint in the CAR is the one the group fixes.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What the clause chooses; proved.)} The untwisted family ($a_{1}, a_{2}$ with the $b_{p}$) generates the same group $G$, with the same squares, since the pair parity is $-\gamma_{5}\gamma_{6}\cdots\gamma_{10} \in G$ and the untwisted slot Majoranas are the twisted ones times it; but its $24$ slot-pair pairs commute, so it is not a family of signed directions. The content of clause (f) beyond (F2) and (F3) is the choice of the ten directions inside $G$, canonical on $V$ up to a central unit (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv)).
\item[(v)] \emph{(Computed.)} In the occupation basis of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$: $|G| = 2048$, $-1$ central, all $90$ ordered pairs of distinct twisted directions anticommuting, squares $1, -1$ alternating, the $1023$ nonempty blades traceless and the $1024$ blades distinct up to sign; $\tfrac12(\gamma_{2k-1} \pm \gamma_{2k})$ equal to the Fock operators, adjoint to each other, with the $50$ relations of the CAR; $g^{\mathsf T} = g^{-1}$ on all $2048$ elements; commutant of dimension $1$ (and $2$ for nine directions); the untwisted family generating $G$ with all $24$ cross pairs commuting; blade squares equal to GA's for the sign vector $(1, -1, \dots)$, Gauss sum $32$, against $32$ for $(10,0)$ and $-32$ for $(0,10)$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} Once the ten Klein-twisted slot and pair Majoranas are declared the directions (the postulates do not choose them, (iv)), clause (f) is the instance $n = 10$ of Premises (F2) and (F3); Premise (F1) enters only as the index set, the configurations $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{10} = G/\langle c\rangle$ of the ten direction labels, not the $2^{5}$ occupation configurations of $V$, and reading these labels as the foundation's distinctions is a reading, not a theorem; it asks for no adjoint and no signature beyond what the modes and the group supply. Together with the Klein-convention result, the clause has no content on $V$ beyond a choice of directions fixed up to a central unit.

## technical
Clause (f) of the slot-module premise asks that the slot and pair operators form one system of five fermionic modes, the slot operators anticommuting with the pair operators. Written in their ten real Majorana combinations, the anticommutation relations of five modes are exactly the relations of a group of signed directions, the foundation's minimal non-commutativity premise for ten directions, with the sign bit acting as minus one: distinct directions anticommute, and each mode supplies one direction squaring to one and one squaring to the sign. The group has order $2^{11}$ and its blades are trace-orthogonal, so the integer Clifford algebra of signature $(5,5)$ acts faithfully, and its Gauss sum puts it in the class of $(10,0)$. Neither an adjoint nor a signature is extra: the Fock adjoint is the group inverse, the invariant form is unique up to scale, and the signature comes from the modes. The untwisted slot operators generate the same group but commute with the pairs, so the clause's only content is which ten elements of the group are the directions, which the Klein convention fixes up to a central unit.

## lay
One assumption of the series about how a composite particle's internal states are built says that two families of internal switches, the slot and pair switches, behave as one combined set of fermionic switches. The series' foundation starts from even simpler assumptions: independent yes-or-no distinctions, which become directions whose order matters by a single sign. This result shows that, once ten particular combinations of the switches are chosen as the directions, the assumption about the switches is exactly the foundation's assumption about directions applied to those ten, and nothing more: the rule for adjoints and the pattern of squares that the assumption seems to need are already supplied by the directions themselves. What the assumption fixes is only which ten elements of a given group are called directions, a choice made canonical earlier.

## one-liner
On the composite space, the CAR of the five slot and pair modes are exactly Premise (F2) for their ten Majoranas with the sign bit $-1$ (order $2^{11}$, signature $(5,5)$, Gauss sum $2^{5}$ as for $(10,0)$); the Fock adjoint is the group inverse and the invariant form unique; the untwisted operators generate the same group but are not signed directions: once the twisted Majoranas are declared the directions (a choice the postulates do not make), clause (f) is an instance of (F2) and (F3), (F1) entering only as the index set.

proofs.proof-main.tex:
\emph{Setting.} $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ with $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$ is the composite space of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}, with its Fock inner product (Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.fock-representation}); there the Klein-twisted slot operators $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}$ and the pair operators $b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, with adjoints the Fock adjoints (its (i), (ii)), and the untwisted $a_{i}$ commute with the $b_{p}$. In the occupation basis of $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ these are the Jordan-Wigner operators of five modes (slots first), and the check works there: $\Lambda^{\bullet}\C^{5}$ has the rational occupation basis and every Majorana combination below is a signed permutation matrix in it, so all statements are about real matrices and need no imaginary unit.

\emph{(i).} Write $\gamma = \alpha + \alpha^{*}$, $\gamma' = \alpha - \alpha^{*}$ for each mode, so $\alpha = \tfrac12(\gamma + \gamma')$, $\alpha^{*} = \tfrac12(\gamma - \gamma')$. Then $\gamma^{2} = \alpha^{2} + \alpha^{*2} + \{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\}$, $\gamma'^{2} = \alpha^{2} + \alpha^{*2} - \{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\}$ and $\{\gamma, \gamma'\} = 2(\alpha^{2} - \alpha^{*2})$, and for two modes $\alpha$, $\beta$ the four anticommutators of $\gamma_{\alpha}, \gamma'_{\alpha}$ with $\gamma_{\beta}, \gamma'_{\beta}$ are the images of $\{\alpha, \beta\}$, $\{\alpha, \beta^{*}\}$, $\{\alpha^{*}, \beta\}$, $\{\alpha^{*}, \beta^{*}\}$ under an invertible linear map (the change of basis above, applied to each factor). So the CAR ($\alpha^{2} = 0$, $\{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\} = 1$, cross anticommutators zero, and the relations with $\alpha^{*}$ obtained by taking adjoints) hold exactly when $\gamma^{2} = 1$, $\gamma'^{2} = -1$ for every mode and every two distinct Majoranas anticommute. On $V$, $-1$ is central with square $1$. If the CAR hold, the group $G$ generated by the ten $\gamma$'s and $-1$ consists of the $\pm\gamma_{S}$, $\gamma_{S}$ the increasing products; a nonempty $\gamma_{S}$ is traceless on $V$ (it anticommutes with an invertible $\gamma_{j}$, $j \notin S$ when $|S|$ is odd, which exists since $|S| < 10$, and $j \in S$ when $|S|$ is even, so $\operatorname{tr}\gamma_{S} = \operatorname{tr}(\gamma_{j}^{-1}\gamma_{S}\gamma_{j}) = -\operatorname{tr}\gamma_{S}$), while $\pm1$ has trace $\pm32$, so no nonempty $\gamma_{S}$ is $\pm1$ and the $\gamma_{S}$ are pairwise trace-orthogonal ($\gamma_{S}^{-1}\gamma_{T} = \pm\gamma_{S \triangle T}$). Hence $G/\{\pm1\}$ is elementary abelian of order $2^{10}$ with basis the images of the $\gamma$'s, distinct directions satisfy $\gamma_{i}\gamma_{j} = (-1)\gamma_{j}\gamma_{i}$, and $-1 \ne 1$: (F2) holds for the ten directions with $c = -1$ and $e_{i}^{2} = c^{s_{i}}$, $s = (0, 1, 0, 1, \dots)$, and the representation of $\Z[G]$ on $V$ sends $c$ to $-1$, so it factors through $A = \Z[G]/(c + 1)$ (F3). By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(v), (vii), $A = \Cl_{\Z}(5,5)$, and it acts faithfully on $V$ by trace-orthogonality of the blades. Conversely, if the ten operators with $-1$ form a group of signed directions with these squares, the identities above give the CAR for $\tfrac12(\gamma + \gamma')$ and $\tfrac12(\gamma - \gamma')$; the factor $\tfrac12$ needs the rationals, which the coefficients of the operators on $V$ already are. For the given modes the CAR hold (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(ii), and Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.witt-basis-car} for each Fock system), so the twisted slot and pair Majoranas are a group of signed directions of order $2^{11}$, which the check confirms directly: closure of order $2048$, the $90$ ordered pairs of distinct directions anticommuting, the squares alternating, the $1023$ nonempty blades traceless, the $1024$ blades distinct up to sign, and the recovered $\tfrac12(\gamma \pm \gamma')$ equal to the Fock operators and satisfying the $50$ relations of the CAR. The two sign bits of the slot and pair systems are both the operator $-1$ of $V$, so sharing one sign bit is automatic on $V$; what (F2) adds to the two separate systems is the anticommutation of the $24$ slot-pair pairs.

\emph{(ii).} (F2) leaves the signature free, but a mode determines it: $\alpha^{2} = 0$ and $\{\alpha, \alpha^{*}\} = 1$ give $\gamma^{2} = 1$ and $\gamma'^{2} = -1$, so five modes give the signature $(5,5)$ and nothing in the clause chooses it. The check computes the squares of all $1024$ blades as operators, finds them equal to GA's blade squares for the sign vector $(1, -1, \dots)$ (the quadratic form $q$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}), and the Gauss sum $\sum_{S}\gamma_{S}^{2} = 32 = 2^{5}$, the value of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra}(viii) for $p - q \equiv 0, 2 \pmod 8$, shared with $(10,0)$ (also $32$) and not with $(0,10)$ ($-32$); so $\Cl_{\Z}(5,5) \cong \Cl_{\Z}(10,0)$ by (viii), the class of the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f) (whose generators over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ are the five $\gamma$'s and the five $I_{4}\gamma'$'s, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(ii)).

\emph{(iii).} $\gamma^{*} = \gamma = \gamma^{-1}$ and $\gamma'^{*} = \alpha^{*} - \alpha = -\gamma' = \gamma'^{-1}$; the adjoint and the inversion are both anti-automorphisms of $G$ agreeing on generators, so $g^{*} = g^{-1}$ on all of $G$ (the check confirms it on all $2048$ elements, as transposes of signed permutation matrices). The inversion $g \mapsto g^{-1}$ of $\Z[G]$ fixes $c$, hence preserves $(c + 1)$ and descends to an anti-involution of $A$: the adjoint on the image of $A$ is the group's own inversion. A symmetric bilinear form $B$ on the rational span of the occupation basis is $G$-invariant ($g^{\mathsf T}Bg = B$) exactly when $B$ commutes with $G$, since $g^{\mathsf T} = g^{-1}$; the check computes the commutant of the ten Majoranas in $M_{32}(\Q)$ by a signed union-find on the entries ($K_{\pi(i)\pi(j)} = s_{i}s_{j}K_{ij}$ for each signed permutation) and finds it one-dimensional (two-dimensional for nine of them, the control). So the $G$-invariant form is the Fock form up to a scalar, and the adjoint used in the CAR is the one the group fixes.

\emph{(iv).} The pair parity $P = (-1)^{k}$ commutes with the slot operators and anticommutes with the pair operators, and for each mode $\gamma\gamma' = (\alpha + \alpha^{*})(\alpha - \alpha^{*}) = \alpha^{*}\alpha - \alpha\alpha^{*} = -(-1)^{n}$, so $P = -\gamma_{5}\gamma_{6}\cdots\gamma_{10}$ (the six pair Majoranas) lies in $G$. The untwisted slot Majoranas are $\gamma_{i}P$ ($i \le 4$): they lie in $G$, have the same squares ($(\gamma_{i}P)^{2} = \gamma_{i}^{2}P^{2} = \gamma_{i}^{2}$) and commute with every pair Majorana. So the untwisted family generates a subgroup of $G$ of order $2^{11}$ (the check computes it), which is $G$ itself, but it is not a family of signed directions: the $24$ slot-pair pairs commute and (F2c) fails. The group, its sign bit, its signature and its inversion are therefore the same in both conventions, and the content of clause (f) beyond (F2) and (F3) is the choice of which ten elements of $G$ are the directions; by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space}(iv) that choice is canonical on $V$ up to a central unit. This is the extraspecial central product $2^{1+4}\circ 2^{1+6} \cong 2^{1+10}$ of the slot and pair groups, read with two different generating sets (prior art; not used).

\emph{Status.} Transport-absent. (F1) enters only as the index set $\mathbb{F}_{2}^{10} = G/\langle c\rangle$ of the ten direction labels (not the $2^{5}$ occupation configurations of $V$); identifying these labels with the foundation's distinctions is a reading. The equivalence of the CAR with the Clifford relations of the Majoranas in (i) is classical (Jordan and Wigner), derived here for completeness. Nothing here derives clause (f) from tower structure; it shows that, on $V$, the clause is the statement of Premises (F2) and (F3) for the ten slot and pair Majorana directions, with no further content.

check_py:
"""synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-an-instance-of-the-signed-direction-postulates: exact checks.

V = Lambda C^5 in the occupation (bitmask) basis of lib/fock.py, modes 0, 1 the slots and 2, 3, 4 the pairs. The
Jordan-Wigner operators a_k (fock.ann, fock.cre) are the Klein-twisted slot operators and the pair operators of
synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space: one five-mode system. The untwisted
slot operators are a_i (-1)^k with (-1)^k the pair parity. Real Majoranas (fock.majorana, kind 'real'):
gamma_{2k} = a_k^dag + a_k (square +1), gamma_{2k+1} = a_k - a_k^dag (square -1). Every product of Majoranas is a
signed permutation matrix on the 32 states, stored as a tuple col -> (row, sign).
"""
from fractions import Fraction as F

import GA
import fock
from tp_premise import premise

NM = 5
DIM = 1 << NM
SLOT_MAJ = 4
PAIR_MODES = [2, 3, 4]


def mono(M):
    out = [None] * DIM
    for (r, c), v in M.items():
        if out[c] is not None or v not in (1, -1):
            return None
        out[c] = (r, int(v))
    return tuple(out) if all(x is not None for x in out) else None


def mmul(A, B):
    return tuple((A[B[j][0]][0], A[B[j][0]][1] * B[j][1]) for j in range(DIM))


IDN = tuple((j, 1) for j in range(DIM))
NEG = tuple((j, -1) for j in range(DIM))


def neg(A):
    return mmul(NEG, A)


def transpose(A):
    out = [None] * DIM
    for j in range(DIM):
        r, s = A[j]
        out[r] = (j, s)
    return tuple(out)


def trace(A):
    return sum(A[j][1] for j in range(DIM) if A[j][0] == j)


def twisted():
    return [mono(fock.majorana(p, NM)) for p in range(2 * NM)]


def pair_parity():
    return mono(fock.parity(NM, modes=PAIR_MODES))


def untwisted():
    tw, P = twisted(), pair_parity()
    return [mmul(tw[p], P) if p < SLOT_MAJ else tw[p] for p in range(2 * NM)]


def group(gens):
    G = {IDN}
    frontier = [IDN]
    while frontier:
        nf = []
        for g in frontier:
            for h in gens:
                x = mmul(g, h)
                if x not in G:
                    G.add(x)
                    nf.append(x)
        frontier = nf
    return G


def relation(A, B):
    """+1 if A, B commute, -1 if they anticommute, 0 otherwise"""
    ab, ba = mmul(A, B), mmul(B, A)
    return 1 if ab == ba else -1 if ab == neg(ba) else 0


def square_sign(A):
    s = mmul(A, A)
    return 1 if s == IDN else -1 if s == NEG else 0


def blade(gens, S):
    out = IDN
    for i in sorted(S):
        out = mmul(out, gens[i])
    return out


def subsets(n):
    return [tuple(i for i in range(n) if m >> i & 1) for m in range(1 << n)]


def run_directions(gens):
    """(group order, c central, off-diagonal relations, squares, nonempty blades traceless, blades distinct mod sign)"""
    G = group(gens + [NEG])
    central = all(mmul(g, NEG) == mmul(NEG, g) for g in G) and NEG in G and NEG != IDN
    rels = sorted(set(relation(gens[i], gens[j]) for i in range(len(gens)) for j in range(len(gens)) if i != j))
    sq = [square_sign(g) for g in gens]
    blades = [blade(gens, S) for S in subsets(len(gens))]
    traceless = all(trace(b) == 0 for b in blades[1:]) and trace(blades[0]) == DIM
    classes = set(min(b, neg(b)) for b in blades)
    return len(G), central, rels, sq, traceless, len(classes)


def run_car_from_directions():
    """modes recovered as a_k = (gamma_{2k} + gamma_{2k+1})/2, adjoint (gamma_{2k} - gamma_{2k+1})/2: (failures of
    equality with the Fock operators, failures of the CAR)"""
    gam = [fock.majorana(p, NM) for p in range(2 * NM)]
    half = F(1, 2)
    eq_bad = car_bad = 0
    a = [fock.msc(half, fock.madd(gam[2 * k], gam[2 * k + 1])) for k in range(NM)]
    ad = [fock.msc(half, fock.msub(gam[2 * k], gam[2 * k + 1])) for k in range(NM)]
    for k in range(NM):
        eq_bad += 0 if fock.meq(a[k], fock.ann(k, NM)) and fock.meq(ad[k], fock.cre(k, NM)) else 1
        eq_bad += 0 if fock.meq(ad[k], fock.dag(a[k])) else 1
    one = fock.eye(DIM)
    for k in range(NM):
        for l in range(NM):
            car_bad += 0 if fock.meq(fock.acomm(a[k], ad[l]), one if k == l else {}) else 1
            car_bad += 0 if fock.is_zero(fock.acomm(a[k], a[l])) else 1
    return eq_bad, car_bad


def inverse(g):
    s = square_sign(g)
    return g if s == 1 else neg(g)


def commutant_dim(gens):
    """dimension of {K in M(32, Q) : g K g^-1 = K for every g in gens}, by signed union-find on the entries"""
    parent = {}
    par = {}

    def find(x):
        if parent[x] == x:
            return x, 0
        r, p = find(parent[x])
        parent[x] = r
        par[x] = (par[x] + p) % 2
        return r, par[x]
    dead = set()
    for i in range(DIM):
        for j in range(DIM):
            parent[(i, j)] = (i, j)
            par[(i, j)] = 0
    for g in gens:
        for i in range(DIM):
            for j in range(DIM):
                # (g K g^-1)_{pi(i) pi(j)} = s_i s_j K_ij, so K_{pi(i) pi(j)} = s_i s_j K_ij
                (pi, si), (pj, sj) = g[i], g[j]
                flip = 0 if si * sj == 1 else 1
                ra, pa = find((i, j))
                rb, pb = find((pi, pj))
                if ra == rb:
                    if (pa + pb + flip) % 2:
                        dead.add(ra)
                else:
                    parent[ra] = rb
                    par[ra] = (pa + pb + flip) % 2
    roots = set()
    for x in list(parent):
        r, _ = find(x)
        roots.add(r)
    dead_roots = set(find(d)[0] for d in dead)
    return len(roots - dead_roots)


def run_adjoint():
    tw = twisted()
    G = group(tw + [NEG])
    adj_is_inverse = sum(1 for g in G if transpose(g) == inverse(g))
    return len(G), adj_is_inverse, commutant_dim(tw), commutant_dim(tw[:-1])


def run_untwisted():
    tw, ut = twisted(), untwisted()
    G, G0 = group(tw + [NEG]), group(ut + [NEG])
    cross = [relation(ut[i], ut[j]) for i in range(SLOT_MAJ) for j in range(SLOT_MAJ, 2 * NM)]
    prod_pairs = blade(tw, range(SLOT_MAJ, 2 * NM))
    P = pair_parity()
    twist_inside = P == prod_pairs or P == neg(prod_pairs)
    return G0 == G, cross.count(1), len(cross), [square_sign(g) for g in ut] == [square_sign(g) for g in tw], \
        twist_inside


def run_gauss():
    """(operator Gauss sum, agreement of operator blade squares with GA blade squares, GA Gauss sums of other
    signatures (10,0) and (0,10))"""
    tw = twisted()
    sq = tuple(square_sign(g) for g in tw)
    ops = 0
    agree = 0
    for S in subsets(2 * NM):
        s = square_sign(blade(tw, S))
        ops += s
        sg, _ = GA.blade_mul(S, S, sq)
        agree += 1 if sg == s else 0

    def ga_sum(squares):
        return sum(GA.blade_mul(S, S, squares)[0] for S in subsets(2 * NM))
    return ops, agree, ga_sum(tuple([1] * (2 * NM))), ga_sum(tuple([-1] * (2 * NM))), sq

def check_majoranas_form_a_group_of_signed_directions():
    """the ten twisted Majoranas and -1 generate a group of order 2^11, -1 central, every two distinct directions
    anticommute, squares +1, -1 alternating, the 1023 nonempty blades traceless and the 1024 blades distinct up to
    sign: (F2) with the sign bit acting as -1 (F3); the untwisted family fails F2c."""
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    order, central, rels, sq, traceless, classes = run_directions(twisted())
    ok = order == 2048 and central and rels == [-1] and sq == [1, -1] * 5 and traceless and classes == 1024
    rels_u = run_directions(untwisted())[2]
    ok = ok and rels_u == [-1, 1]
    GA.check("slot and pair Majoranas with -1: a group of signed directions of order 2^11, signature (5,5)", ok)
    return ok


def check_car_is_equivalent_to_the_direction_relations():
    """a_k = (gamma_{2k} + gamma_{2k+1})/2 and a_k^dag = (gamma_{2k} - gamma_{2k+1})/2 are the Fock operators, the
    second the adjoint of the first, and they satisfy the CAR of one five-mode system (50 relations)."""
    premise("std-algebra.witt-basis-car")
    premise("synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space")
    eq_bad, car_bad = run_car_from_directions()
    ok = eq_bad == 0 and car_bad == 0
    GA.check("the CAR of the five modes are the signed-direction relations of their ten Majoranas", ok)
    return ok


def check_adjoint_is_the_group_inverse_and_the_invariant_form_is_unique():
    """on all 2048 elements of G the Fock adjoint (transpose) is the group inverse; the commutant of G on Q^32 is
    one-dimensional, so the G-invariant symmetric form is the Fock form up to scale; nine Majoranas leave two."""
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    premise("std-algebra.fock-representation")
    order, adj_inv, dim10, dim9 = run_adjoint()
    ok = order == 2048 and adj_inv == 2048 and dim10 == 1 and dim9 == 2
    GA.check("the adjoint of the CAR is the inversion of the group of signed directions; the invariant form is unique",
             ok)
    return ok


def check_untwisted_directions_generate_the_same_group():
    """the untwisted Majoranas generate the same group G with the same squares, but all 24 slot-pair pairs commute;
    the pair parity is +-1 times the product of the six pair Majoranas, an element of G (the Klein twist inside G)."""
    premise("synthesis.joint-clifford-clause-is-a-klein-convention-on-the-composite-space")
    same, commuting, total, same_sq, twist_inside = run_untwisted()
    ok = same and (commuting, total) == (24, 24) and same_sq and twist_inside
    GA.check("untwisted and twisted directions generate one group; only the choice of directions differs", ok)
    return ok


def check_signature_gauss_sum():
    """operator blade squares agree with GA's blade squares for the signature (5,5) on all 1024 blades; the Gauss
    sum is 32 = 2^5, as for (10,0), while (0,10) gives -32."""
    premise("synthesis.signed-directions-and-the-integer-clifford-algebra")
    premise("synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form")
    ops, agree, s100, s010, sq = run_gauss()
    ok = ops == 32 and agree == 1024 and s100 == 32 and s010 == -32 and sq == (1, -1) * 5
    GA.check("Gauss sum of the slot-pair directions 2^5: Cl(5,5) and Cl(10,0) are one class", ok)
    return ok
